sources.title: Royal Botanic Gardens NSW PlantNET — Pinus pinea diagnosis
sources.scope: Selected actual institutional species diagnosis read for broad rounded crown, fissured bark, paired sheathed needles, pendent ovoid cones lacking terminal scale spines and a rudimentary seed wing. Cultivated/naturalized Australian records and uncertain ancient introductions are not mapped as a verified native range.

sources.title: Valdiviesso etal2017 — reproductive phenology of Pinus pinea
sources.scope: Selected actual PDFpages2–4 read; page4/printed65 Figures1–3 including authentic male/female stage photographs viewed. Study concerns grafted trees in three Portuguese plots monitored during2012–2013. Selected mature brown cone opening is context for partial articulation; full reproductive phenology, timing, climate effects, male structures and seed development are not reconstructed or fitted.

sources.title: Loreto etal2000 — primary and secondary needle distinctions
sources.scope: Selected primary Methods and needle-ontogeny passages read through accessible web text. Studied nursery-grown plants had solitary short primary needles distinct from later paired secondary needles with a basal sheath. No gas-exchange, monoterpene or age-specific numerical rates are fitted. Direct local HTML fetch returned403; no local full-paper reading is claimed.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected accessible web text; direct local HTML403

findings.shape: Original radiating umbrella-like crown and tapered woody axes with individually modeled long paired needles and broad selected seed cones. Juvenile solitary primary needles are distinct from these adult secondary needle cues.
findings.surface: Original darker fissured bark, longer paired green needle surfaces and broad brown woody scale forms. Pigment, sheen and relief are authored rather than fitted to measured optics.
findings.movement: The same trunk, branches, leaves and cones remain present. Working sway is small authored external branch deflection with anchored roots; no wind, stiffness, damping or physiological solver. Selected mature woody scale surfaces additionally bend during a monotonic authored study, without measured humidity, force or timing. Full germination and organ-by-organ seed-to-tree development remain unavailable; the adult crown is not resized into a false developmental sequence.

corrections: Replaced the generic sparse conifer tiers with radiating primary axes and a raised flattened umbrella-like crown.
Moved foliage towards terminal shoots and flattened crown endpoints after actual whole-crown comparison.
Added long paired needle/sheath cues and broad selected seed-cone forms; fixed a missing-cone filter found by the focused check.
Added monotonic partial scale bending on the retained cone surfaces; juvenile solitary needles are distinguished in the record and not faked by resizing the adult.
Added separate trunk, needle-bearing shoot and cone inspection.
findings.residual: The umbrella crown remains a selected simplified form, not a measured mature specimen. Cone inspection is partly obscured by retained needles; scale apophyses and seed cavities remain coarse. Bark relief, needle density, tissue optics, age variation and primary-to-secondary needle development remain incomplete.
